display.purpose: The PNR only, one character per ruled cell; 4.5rem under 720px.

route.purpose: Airport codes on the route axis and the fare total; 2rem under 720px.

headline.purpose: Page h1, flight times on rows, ticket status word.

title.purpose: h2, briefing-strip values, row fares, wordmark.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked name of a value: field labels, fact terms, table heads.

shadows.name: active-leg
shadows.purpose: Structural underline for the current masthead nav item. Not elevation.

shadows.name: next-cell
shadows.purpose: Marks the next PNR entry cell while focused.

shadows.name: field-error-ring
shadows.purpose: Doubles the border of an invalid field.

shadows.name: terrain-patch
shadows.purpose: Lifts text off hatching onto solid terrain (4px in notices).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve for every transition and animation.

motion.name: airways-light
motion.purpose: Airways from the chosen origin fade in.

motion.name: airway-draw
motion.purpose: Signature: the chosen airway draws itself origin to destination.

motion.name: airway-box-in
motion.purpose: Route label box appears as the airway lands.

motion.name: pnr-print
motion.purpose: Signature: PNR cells wipe up on magenta and settle to ink after booking.

motion.name: reduced-motion

components.css: .ds-axis { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; max-width: 420px; } .ds-code { font-family: var(--font-chart, Bahnschrift, 'DIN Alternate', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif); font-size: 2.5rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.02em; line-height: 1; color: var(--ink, #15171a); } .ds-line { position: relative; flex: 1; height: 3px; background: var(--magenta, #a51f63); } .ds-line::before, .ds-line::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 50%; width: 9px; height: 9px; border: 2px solid var(--ink, #15171a); border-radius: 50%; background: var(--paper-2, #eae8e0); transform: translateY(-50%); } .ds-line::before { left: -2px; } .ds-line::after { right: -2px; }

components.css: .ds-pnr { display: flex; width: fit-content; border: 2px solid var(--ink, #15171a); background: var(--paper, #f4f3ee); } .ds-pnr span { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 0.78em; height: 1.12em; border-right: 1px solid var(--ink, #15171a); font-family: var(--font-chart, Bahnschrift, 'DIN Alternate', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif); font-size: 6rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--ink, #15171a); } .ds-pnr span:last-child { border-right: none; } .ds-pnr:hover span { animation: ds-pnr-print 520ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) both; } .ds-pnr:hover span:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: 110ms; } .ds-pnr:hover span:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: 220ms; } .ds-pnr:hover span:nth-child(4) { animation-delay: 330ms; } .ds-pnr:hover span:nth-child(5) { animation-delay: 440ms; } .ds-pnr:hover span:nth-child(6) { animation-delay: 550ms; } @keyframes ds-pnr-print { 0% { clip-path: inset(100% 0 0 0); background: #a51f63; color: #fff; } 55% { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0); background: #a51f63; color: #fff; } 100% { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0); background: transparent; color: #15171a; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-pnr:hover span { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Every screen is published the way an aeronautical chart publishes an approach: a ruled briefing strip of facts across the top, a plan view of the route, and one index number that identifies the whole sheet. The ground is pale chart paper, everything is drawn in black ink with 1px ruled boxes and square corners, and labels are small, uppercase and tracked like frequency boxes. Density is that of a working document: many facts, each in its own cell, none floating.

Colour carries meaning the way it does on a chart, never decoration. Magenta is the airway: the route you have chosen and the one thing you can act on. Blue is information. Tan terrain hatching is ground you cannot fly through: sold-out, departed, withdrawn and cancelled. Depth is not simulated; the sheet is flat and structure comes from rules. The system refuses the online-travel-agency arrangement of a gradient hero, a rounded search widget and floating fare cards.

Motion is reserved for two moments: the chosen airway drawing itself between two airports, and the PNR printing into its cells after booking. Both collapse to instant under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Chart-paper ground, black ink, 1px ruled boxes, square corners.
Magenta is the only accent and the only action colour.
Blue means information; tan hatching means unavailable.
Tabular numerals and uppercase tracked chart lettering for every named value.
Every route is drawn on one axis: origin left, destination right, joined by the airway.
The PNR is the sheet's index number: huge, ruled into six cells, never shrinking.
Flat: no elevation shadows, no rounded cards, no gradients as surface.

rules.name: The One Airway Rule
rules.body: Magenta means "this is your route" or "you can act on this". It never decorates, never marks status, and fills at most one main action per screen.

rules.name: The Terrain Rule
rules.body: Anything the backend refuses (sold out, departed, withdrawn, cancelled) is drawn as hatched terrain, with its text lifted onto solid terrain patches so it stays readable. Refusals are never red; red is only for a field the user typed wrong.

rules.name: The Blue Is Information Rule
rules.body: Blue states facts and confirmations. It is never a link, button or route.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can sit in a column (times, seats, fares, flight numbers, PNRs) is set in the chart font with tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Label Names A Value Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked lettering labels a field, fact or panel it sits on. It is never a free-floating tag line above a heading.

rules.name: The Ruled Sheet Rule
rules.body: If something needs separating, rule it. Never float it on a shadow.

dos: Do rule every box with a 1px ink hairline and keep every corner square (0px).
Do reserve magenta for the chosen route and the single main action on a screen.
Do mark every backend refusal (sold out, departed, withdrawn, cancelled) with terrain hatching and keep its text on solid terrain patches.
Do draw every route on one axis, origin left and destination right, joined by the airway line with a hollow fix at each end.
Do set times, fares, seats and PNRs in the chart font with tabular numerals.
Do keep the PNR at display size in six ruled cells on every ticket view.
Do disable the airway draw and PNR print under prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't use drop shadows, elevation or floating cards; separate with rules and tonal panels.
Don't round the corners of boxes, buttons, fields or tags; circles belong only to chart symbols.
Don't use gradients as a surface or backdrop; the only repeating gradient is the terrain hatch.
Don't use magenta for status or decoration, or blue for anything clickable.
Don't show a backend refusal in red; red is for a field the user typed wrong.
Don't shrink, truncate or restyle the PNR to fit a layout.
